## Verdict: the audit **SEES** a governed-surface PR that lands through a merge-queue batch

Measured, not reasoned from the gate's source. Every batch topology below lists the governed file; **zero of six batch topologies are blind**. Per this card's disposition rule that confirms the post-hoc-audit model (2026-08-18 ruling) covers the queue route, so **no code changed and no PR opened**. Closing is left to PM review.

Branch `claude/issue-11996-governed-merges-queue-batch` carries no commits, deliberately.

---

### 1. What a queue batch on this repo actually looks like (measured live, not assumed)

A real batch was in flight during the measurement:

```
$ git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/*'
4be2e880e7…  refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-12622-cbacc9691c…
cbacc9691c…  refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-12625-0043c92240…
aa5994e17a…  refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-12626-4be2e880e7…
```

The branch names pair each entry to the sha it stacks on, and the chain that produces is:

```
$ git log --graph --format='%h [%p] %s' aa5994e17a --not 0043c92240
* aa5994e1 [4be2e880] feat(spec): Operation Message Catalog gains refusal-situation keys … (#12626)
* 4be2e880 [cbacc969] test(cli): make the app-anchored serve e2e prove a BOOT, not just a resolution (#12622)
* cbacc969 [0043c922] test(rest): pay down 17 of the test-typecheck ledger's 37 errors (#12625)
```

So the batch signature here is: **one single-parent squash commit per PR, stacked on the previous entry, committer `GitHub`, subject ending in the trailing `(#N)` parenthetical**; `main` then fast-forwards to the batch tip. Confirmed end-to-end mid-measurement — `origin/main` moved `0043c9224 -> 4be2e880e` while this work was running, i.e. the very commits fetched above from the queue branch became `main` by fast-forward.

Corroborating the shape across history, on 3613 first-parent commits of `main`:

- **zero** multi-parent commits on the first-parent chain;
- committer is `GitHub` on 2001 of 2002 sampled;
- 533 of 2001 consecutive pairs land within 60 s of each other — batches, not 533 hand merges.

That matters because it settles which topology is the live one rather than leaving it to inference.

### 2. Real-history replay: the real sweep over a real batch carrying two governed PRs

A real 5-commit / 24-second batch on 2026-08-26 contained two governed landings. Running the gate unmodified:

```
$ node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --repos objectstack --since 2026-08-26T05:00:26Z
governed-merges sweep: 3 governed merge(s) since 2026-08-26T05:00:26.000Z across 1/1 governed repo(s)
  scanned 75 mainline commit(s); 3 API lookup(s).
  • objectstack-ai/objectstack PR #12443 — docs(pm-dispatch): repo-class governance split … (#12443)
      commit ade757fb3 @ 2026-08-26T05:00:49+00:00
      surfaces: .claude/** ×2
        - .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md
        - .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/decision-analysis.md
  • objectstack-ai/objectstack PR #12440 — Reconcile os-dev contract and pm-dispatch channel references … (#12440)
      commit 04600d939 @ 2026-08-26T05:00:27+00:00
      surfaces: .claude/** ×3
        - .claude/agents/os-dev.md
        - .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md
        - .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/rest-channel.md
EXIT=2
```

Both governed queue landings are listed, with the right PR numbers and the right file lists. `EXIT=2` is the attribution leg only — every channel answered HTTP 403 at this container's proxy, which the gate classifies as an ENVIRONMENT problem and prints as `merged_by UNAVAILABLE`. It is not a missed entry; the entries are on the list.

### 3. Constructed-signature matrix

Because the live queue only produces one topology, the rest were constructed: throwaway repos carrying each merge-queue batch shape, each landing the **same** governed edit (`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`, PR #22222) and differing **only** in the topology it arrives by, then swept by the real script via `--repo-root objectstack=PATH`. Attribution was pointed at a dead endpoint so the run measures enumeration, not network.

| topology | what it is | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **QS-1** squash-batch | shape replay of the LIVE signature in section 1 | **SEES** — listed, attributed to the governed PR |
| **QS-2** merge-commit batch | queue with the merge-commit method: one two-parent merge per PR, ff onto main | **SEES** — listed, attributed to the governed PR |
| **QS-3** single-batch-merge | main advances by ONE two-parent merge whose second parent is the whole queue chain | **SEES the file**, attributes it to #11111 (the PR named in the merge subject) |
| **QS-4** octopus-batch-merge | one commit, N parents, governed inside a non-first parent | **SEES the file**, `pr: null` — listed as its own loud entry |
| **QS-5** rebase-batch | linear, original author dates preserved, committer dates at landing | **SEES** — listed, attributed to the governed PR |
| **QS-6** same-second batch at the boundary | whole batch shares one committer second and `--since` is set to exactly that second | **SEES** — listed, attributed to the governed PR |

**Blind topologies: 0.** The governed **file** reaches the list in all six.

The two collapse shapes deserve their qualification stated rather than buried: in QS-3 and QS-4 the governed file is listed but the PR column is wrong or empty. That does not defeat the audit's contract — the list's question is "does the maintainer recognise every entry", and a governed surface with a `.claude/**` file on it is exactly what prompts that recognition; `pullNumberFromSubject` is a convenience column, and the header already rules that a mainline commit naming no PR "is listed as its own loud entry". It is also not a live gap: **this repo's queue does not produce either shape** (section 1). Recording them so a future merge-method change is a known quantity, not a surprise.

### 4. `merged_at` collapse and `merged_by` semantics

- **`merged_at` is display-only.** It is read once into `attribution.mergedAt` and rendered once in the report line; it is used in no filter, no key and no dedupe. The window is cut on the commit's committer date by `git log --since`, never on `merged_at`. So a batch collapsing several PRs onto one merge timestamp cannot cost the list an entry.
- **`merged_by` read `os-steve` for both** governed queue landings in section 2 — a seat account, not the maintainer's. Per the header's own 2026-08-18 caveat that is not by itself the violation signal: `merged_by` names an ACCOUNT, not a PRINCIPAL, and the maintainer also operates the seat accounts. Recording it verbatim as the header instructs. This is the first reading on this repo that is not `hotlong`, so the header's "if a future reading shows a bot login" note is worth widening to "a login other than the maintainer's" — but no bot login appeared, so no remap is proposed.

### 5. Baseline

`node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --self-test` under the shared verify lock:

```
✓ check-governed-merges --self-test: 157 assertions (…)
  live: no generator toolchain in this environment (the generator's own --check exited 254) — the row failed closed, which is the ruled answer here
os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 1s · waited 0s
```

Note for the record: this card says "129 assertions green today". The current count is **157** — the register grew between filing and dispatch. Nothing in this card changed it.

### 6. One thing the measurement turned up that is NOT this card's question

The queue writes an entry's commit at **build** time and marks the PR merged at **land** time — measured here as a 25 to 32 minute skew (#12440 commit 05:00:27Z vs `merged_at` 05:25:22Z; #12443 commit 05:00:49Z vs 05:33:08Z). That puts 10 committer-date inversions on `main`'s first-parent chain in the last 3612 pairs, **two of them governed**, and a `--since` boundary landing inside such an inversion drops the governed entry with nothing marking the gap.

That is a property of the sweep's **window**, not of the batch **topology** this card asks about, and it does not open under the documented default (`--since 24h`; the largest measured skew is 1.012% of that window). So it is filed rather than fixed here: **#12633**, with the evidence and four options.

### 7. Reproducing this

Sections 1, 2, 4 and 6 need no rig — they are `git`/`gh`-free commands against this repo plus two PR reads, and every command is quoted above. Section 3's constructed repos came from a throwaway harness (single file, `git commit-tree` plumbing, ~250 lines) that was **not** committed, since this card's disposition rule forbids a code change on a "sees" verdict. If PM wants that matrix to stay covered as a pin, that is a follow-up worth ruling on — say so and it can ride its own card.

Two container-level notes for PM that no field covers:

- **A `git fetch --depth=N` re-shallows the whole shared object store, every sibling worktree included.** Fetching the live queue branches with `--depth=25` collapsed this clone's visible history from 2002 commits to 50. The gate's own horizon guard is what caught it — it refused the sweep with "this clone is shallow and its oldest visible commit on 'origin/main' is 2026-08-26, which sits INSIDE the window" rather than under-reporting into a short list that reads as compliance. Repaired with `git fetch --shallow-since=2026-08-01 origin main` (now 3613 first-parent commits) and left deep, since deeper only helps siblings. Worth knowing before anyone reaches for `--depth` in a shared checkout.
- **Channel:** repo-scoped REST answered HTTP 403 from this container and `gh` is absent, so dedupe went through one targeted MCP `search_issues` instead, with #11996 itself as the same-query control term to prove the channel was live rather than merely quiet. No duplicate of #12633 existed among the 19 results.

Probe refs created during the measurement were deleted; the worktree is removed. The branch is left in place with zero commits because both claim comments name it.

Acceptance criterion met: a written verdict (SEES — zero blind topologies of six, live-batch replay + constructed-signature matrix) either way, backed by the runs quoted on this card.

Open-question ruling (verification strategy — named seat-discretion class): **C, land nothing now.** The measurement itself shows the enumeration is robust by construction (even the two collapse shapes list the governed file; only the convenience PR column degrades), the decay scenario requires a maintainer-side merge-method change, and a new git-I/O gate in the farm for a property with zero live pull fails the startup-focus test. The durable record is one header note — topology verdict, dated, with the re-measure trigger (merge-method change, or a refactor of the mainline-commits/commit-paths enumeration) — riding #12633's already-authorized edit of this same script; recorded on that card as a rider.
